newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Enterprise set for firm profit rise.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Enterprise set for firm profit rise.

text.p: Higher oil prices and increased production will have fuelled Enterprise Oil Plc's profits substantially higher, analysts said ahead of the firm's 1996 results' release on Thursday.
They forecast annual profit after tax between 142.6 million and 157.0 million stg, compared with 101.6 million stg the previous year.
Some industry watchers also expect a dividend increase to 17 pence from 16 to mark Enterprise's sound performance last year.
A flow of good news on new oil finds helped the company regain investor confidence in 1996, when Enterprise shares outshone all other FTSE 100 companies.
Enterprise's failed bid three years ago for rival Lasmo had badly hurt the company's reputation but all is forgotten now.
The company has promising exploration projects in Italy, Denmark and Norway and late last year also made inroads in the Gulf of Mexico.
Enterprise announced a Gulf of Mexico alliance with Pennzoil in September and the partners already reported an oil find in January.
Analysts expect average production of 250,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in 1996 and see that rise to about 300,000 by around 1999.
"Put all this together and you've got a pretty good story," said one leading analyst, who expects the pay-out to be raised.

The fact Graham Hearne handed over the helm to new chief executive Pierre Jungels at the start of this year may be another incentive for Enterprise to hike the pay-out to mark the end of a successful year, the analyst added.
